prompt: Built-in imagegen: nine natural-fork prehistoric finds in a square 3x3 warm-ivory paper and matte-gouache swatch. Cells: twig spanning root opening, leaf soot impression on split rock, loose root nest in fallen tree fork, stones at soft earth anvil, quick-release knot at branch crotch, charcoal smudge on cave rock, chip repairing shell rim, wood curl saved beside charcoal, ochre-thumbprint handstone passed between hands.

entries.review: Top-left: thin unmarked twig caught across the natural opening between two roots.
Top-middle: black leaf-shaped soot impression on split stone with decaying leaf beside it.
Top-right: loose free-ended roots gathered as a shallow nest in a fallen-tree fork, before weaving.
Middle-left: hard handstone and a softer battered clay-and-earth anvil together in a root hollow.
Middle-middle: rough fiber quick-release knot around a branch crotch with a long loose pull tail.
Middle-right: amorphous charcoal mark matching a natural shadow on rough cave rock, without symbols.
Bottom-left: damaged shell with a single jagged stone chip wedged at its broken rim.
Bottom-middle: pale raw wood curl protected in a bark split beside charcoal crumbs.
Bottom-right: rough handstone being passed between working hands, marked by one ochre thumb smear.
